text:
maya: heads-up — CI perf alert on PR 5490, microbench batcher_latency jumped ~18% on linux-x86 runners. failing test: tests/perf/test_batch_wait.py::test_prefix_kv_hit_throughput
jonathan: saw the alert, do we have the raw bench output?
samira: linking the CI job: https://ci.internal.redwood/5490/bench-3/output (copied relevant lines below)
perf-ci-bot: benchmark diff summary:
  - batcher_latency p50: baseline=12.3ms new=14.6ms (+18.7%)
  - token_throughput: baseline=11.2k tok/s new=9.1k tok/s (-18.8%)
  - kv_cache_hitrate: baseline=72.1% new=54.6% (-17.5%)
jonathan: kv hitrate drop is the big red flag — suggests more cache churn with the new batching heuristics in the PR
maya: PR 5490 changed adaptive_batching threshold logic and added a heuristic to split long sequences earlier (commit: feat/batching-adaptive-threshold @ abcdef1)
samira: I ran a local microbench with --flame and got a small perf profile. hot stacks (aggregated):
  45% Batcher::wait_for_fill
  20% KernelSelector::choose_kernel
  12% KVCache::evict_if_needed
  8% quantized_gemm::run
  5% memcpy (device->host)
  (flame snippet pasted below)
```
Batcher::wait_for_fill
  KernelSelector::choose_kernel
    AdaptivePolicy::should_split
      KVCache::lookup
        KVCache::evict_if_needed
```
jonathan: eviction showing up in hot path — adaptive splitting may be generating many smaller requests that miss the prefix cache and trigger evictions
luca: can you paste the microbench command and the env? we need to reproduce on CI image (cuda/torch pinned)
samira: command: `pytest tests/perf/test_batch_wait.py -k prefix_kv_hit_throughput -q --bench --bench-flame --runs=5`
env: CUDA=11.8, TORCH=2.2.1, runtime-build=2026-03-01, kernel-abi=v3
perf-ci-bot: added raw logfile: /artifacts/5490/bench.log (kv_lookup latencies spiking, many small writes to cache metadata)
maya: quick bisect plan: revert the adaptive split change in the PR and run microbench on CI. if that fixes kv_hitrate and latency then we revert and iterate on less aggressive thresholding
jonathan: I can try a local revert test now — patch: `git revert --no-commit abcdef1` and run bench in docker image
samira: while jonathan runs that, I also instrumented counters in KVCache: increased eviction_count from ~1500 to ~8400 across 1000 requests with PR applied
luca: that's huge, we should hold the rollout. i'll flag the PR as rollout-blocker in the release board and add "hold" label
maya: +1 hold. Also add perf regression note to the PR with these numbers so reviewers are aware
jonathan: local revert results: p50 down to 12.6ms, throughput back to 10.9k tok/s, kv_hitrate ~71%. Looks like revert fixes it.
samira: bisect narrowed it to the adaptive split heuristic — specifically the branch that shrinks max_batch_window for sequences >512 tokens
maya: suggestion: revert for now, open a follow-up that adds a gated experiment and increases cache-friendly batching tests (include KV hitrate assertions in perf unit tests)
luca: I'll raise the revert PR and tag ops for an expedited canary rollback if the main branch got rolled out.
perf-ci-bot: created issue perf/5490-batcher-kv-regress and attached bench artifacts
jonathan: leaving notes on PR: repro steps, flame output, counter dumps, and a minimal repro script `tools/repro/repro_batch_kv_thrash.py`
samira: minimal repro uses synthetic request stream with many long-prefixed sequences to exercise split path
maya: thanks all. after revert lands let's run an extended perf suite and add an integration test asserting kv_hitrate doesn't drop more than 5% vs baseline for representative workloads
luca: assigning follow-up to samira and jonathan to prototype a less cache-destructive split policy and add unit tests
maya: ack. will monitor CI and update release board. :eyes:
